title: SPARK CSEC Mathematics - Paper 02 Practice Paper B

instructions: This paper consists of THREE sections: I, II and III.
Section I has THREE questions; Section II has THREE questions and Section III has THREE questions.
Numerical answers that are non-exact should be given correct to 3 significant figures or 1 decimal place for angles in degrees, unless a different level of accuracy is specified in the question.

questions.topic: Computation in standard form, currency exchange and consumer arithmetic

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
Determine the value of the following, giving your answer in standard form.

(0.36 x 0.055)/sqrt(0.09 x 25)

criteria.description: the value of the expression
the value written in standard form

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the rates of exchange at a commercial bank in Kingston.

US$1.00 = JA$156.00
CAN$1.00 = JA$120.00

Using the table, calculate the CAN equivalent of US$1.00.

criteria.description: finding the CAN equivalent of JA$1.00
multiplying the CAN equivalent of JA$1.00 by 156.00

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Mr Palmer's daughter, who is a student in Canada, sent him CAN$871.00, which he exchanged for US dollars. Calculate the amount received in US dollars.

criteria.description: dividing by the CAN equivalent of US$1.00

parts.label: (c) (i)
parts.prompt:
Mr Palmer is paid a basic wage of $18.50 per hour for a 40-hour week. Overtime is paid at time-and-a-half. In one week he worked 47 hours.

Calculate his TOTAL wage for that week.
parts.solution: His basic wage is 40 x $18.50 = $740.00. Overtime is paid at 1.5 x $18.50 = $27.75 per hour, and he worked 47 - 40 = 7 hours of overtime, earning 7 x $27.75 = $194.25. His total wage is $740.00 + $194.25 = $934.25.

criteria.description: finding the overtime pay for 7 hours at $27.75 per hour
the total wage

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: In the following week Mr Palmer's total wage was $1 017.50. Determine the TOTAL number of hours that he worked in that week.
parts.solution: His overtime pay was $1 017.50 - $740.00 = $277.50, so the number of hours of overtime is 277.50/27.75 = 10. He therefore worked 40 + 10 = 50 hours in that week.

criteria.description: subtracting the basic wage and dividing by the overtime rate
the total number of hours

questions.stem: Kemar uses matchsticks of length 1 cm to make a row of squares. Figure 1 is a single square, Figure 2 is a row of 2 squares sharing a side, Figure 3 is a row of 3 squares, and the pattern continues.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt:
The table below shows the number of matchsticks used and the perimeter of each figure. Some rows have not been included.

Study the pattern of numbers in each row of the table. Complete the table by filling in the missing information.
parts.solution: The first square uses 4 matchsticks and each further square adds 3, so Figure n uses 3n + 1. Figure 4 uses 3(4) + 1 = 13 and Figure 7 uses 3(7) + 1 = 22. The figure is a 1 cm by n cm rectangle, so its perimeter is 2(n + 1) = 2n + 2: Figure 4 gives 10 cm and Figure 7 gives 16 cm.

mn.description: matchsticks in Figure n, in terms of n

pn.description: perimeter of Figure n, in terms of n

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.prompt: Kemar has 100 matchsticks. Determine the greatest number of squares that can be made in a single row.
parts.solution: 3n + 1 <= 100 gives 3n <= 99, so n <= 33. The greatest whole number of squares is 33, which uses 3(33) + 1 = 100 matchsticks.

criteria.description: forms 3n + 1 <= 100
the greatest number of squares

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.prompt: Write a formula in terms of n for the AREA, in square centimetres, enclosed by Figure n.
parts.solution: Each square encloses 1 cm^2 and Figure n is a row of n squares, so the area enclosed is n cm^2.

criteria.description: the area in terms of n

parts.solution: Both terms have a factor of 2, a factor of x and a factor of y, so the common factor is 2xy. 4x^2y + 10xy^3 = 2xy(2x + 5y^2).

parts.label: (b) (i)
parts.solution: 24 members play a musical instrument and x of them also dance, so the region of M outside D holds 24 - x. In the same way 22 - x members dance but not play a musical instrument, so that goes in the region of D outside M. The x in the overlap and the 3 outside both circles are already shown.

parts.label: (b) (ii)
parts.solution: The four regions account for every one of the 40 members, so (24 - x) + x + (22 - x) + 3 = 40. That is 49 - x = 40, so x = 49 - 40 = 9.

criteria.description: forming the equation (24 - x) + x + (22 - x) + 3 = 40
the value of x

parts.solution: L and M lie on the same horizontal line of the grid, with 4 squares between them, and each square measures 1 cm by 1 cm. So LM = 4 cm on the map.

parts.label: (c) (ii)
parts.prompt: The actual distance between two villages on the island is 618 000 cm. What is this actual distance in km?

criteria.description: the actual distance in kilometres

parts.label: (c) (iii)
parts.prompt: Calculate the ACTUAL area, in km^2, of the forest reserve, given that 1 x 10^10 cm^2 = 1 km^2.
parts.solution: The forest reserve covers 15 of the small squares, so its area on the map is 15 cm^2. The scale is 1 : 20 000, so 1 cm on the map represents 20 000 cm and 1 cm^2 on the map represents 20 000 x 20 000 = 400 000 000 cm^2. The actual area is therefore 15 x 400 000 000 = 6 000 000 000 cm^2, and since 1 x 10^10 cm^2 = 1 km^2 this is 0.6 km^2.

criteria.description: the area of the forest reserve on the map, in cm^2
1 cm^2 on the map represents 20 000 x 20 000 cm^2
the actual area, in km^2
